known_anti_patterns: the bookend tools had zero dedicated checkpoint coverage before this receipt -- session_open/session_status/session_close were only exercised as steps inside session_protocol.rs's longer happy-path chain and its unopened-session refusal test, never as a bookend surface in their own right

session_status has no `goal` field -- the original test draft asserted on one and failed against the live server; the real schema (urn:chatman:ferroplan-session-status:v1) reports cursor, epoch, goal_met, domain_digest, problem_digest, plan_length, remaining_plan_valid, receipt_chain_head instead

a second session_close on an already-closed session_id is NOT a tool-level error -- it returns isError:false with `closed: false` (idempotent no-op), not the `unknown session` refusal that session_status/session_advance/session_observe give on the same closed session_id. The three tools do not converge on one failure mode for post-close reuse; session_close degrades gracefully where the others refuse

negative_falsifier.why_this_counts: opens a session, closes it, then calls session_status on the same now-closed session_id and asserts a tool-level isError:true containing "unknown session" -- not a crash, not a hang, not stale success. It also calls session_close a second time on the same id and asserts the actually-observed idempotent behavior (isError:false, closed:false), which is the opposite of what was first assumed (an `unknown session` refusal); the assertion was corrected to match the live server's real response rather than the guessed one

positive_witness.why_this_counts: opens a session against a small valid STRIPS domain+problem, calls session_status and asserts it echoes the same session_id, reports the domain_digest/problem_digest session_open grounded, goal_met:false and cursor:0 for the fresh unsolved session, then closes it and asserts closed:true -- proving session_open, session_status, and session_close operate on the same underlying session state rather than being independently reachable but disconnected tools

title: Session lifecycle bookends: session_open, session_status, session_close
